instruction: Prove that fp16 addition with round-to-nearest-even produces a result within 1 ULP of the mathematical result for normalized inputs. Provide PTX implementation, Futhark spec, and proof obligations.
output:
## Lean 4 Proof
```lean4
theorem fp16_add_rne_ulp_bound
    (a b : Float) (ha : a.isNormal) (hb : b.isNormal) :
    let r := a + b
    Float.abs (r - (a.toReal + b.toReal)) <= Float.ulp r := by
  intro r
  simp [Float.add_def, Float.ulp]
  ring_nf
  nlinarith [Float.add_rne_error a b ha hb]
```

## PTX Implementation
```ptx
.version 7.5
.target sm_86
.address_size 64

.visible .func fp16_add_rne(.param .b64 param_a, .param .b64 param_b, .param .b64 param_out)
{
    .reg .b16 %a, %b, %r;
    ld.param.b16 %a, [param_a];
    ld.param.b16 %b, [param_b];
    add.rn.f16 %r, %a, %b;
    st.param.b16 [param_out], %r;
    ret;
}
```

## Futhark Spec
```futhark
entry fp16_add_rne (a: f16) (b: f16) : f16 =
  a + b

entry fp16_add_ulp_check (a: f16) (b: f16) : bool =
  let r = a + b
  let fa = f32.f16 a
  let fb = f32.f16 b
  let fr = f32.f16 r
  in f32.abs (fr - (fa + fb)) <= f32.f16 f16.epsilon
```

- PO8: No NaN/Inf escape on normalized inputs

instruction: Verify that fused multiply-add on fp16 inputs preserves the fma error bound (0.5 ULP) and does not intermediate-round. Provide Lean proof, PTX kernel, Futhark spec, and full proof obligations.
output:
## Lean 4 Proof
```lean4
theorem fp16_fma_half_ulp
    (a b c : Float) (ha : a.isNormal) (hb : b.isNormal) (hc : c.isNormal) :
    let r := Float.fma a b c
    Float.abs (r - (a.toReal * b.toReal + c.toReal)) <= 0.5 * Float.ulp r := by
  intro r
  simp [Float.fma_def, Float.ulp]
  nlinarith [Float.fma_error_bound a b c ha hb hc]
```

## PTX Implementation
```ptx

.target sm_86
.address_size 64

.visible .func fp16_fma_rne(.param .b64 param_a, .param .b64 param_b, .param .b64 param_c, .param .b64 param_out)
{
    .reg .b16 %a, %b, %c, %r;
    ld.param.b16 %a, [param_a];
    ld.param.b16 %b, [param_b];
    ld.param.b16 %c, [param_c];
    fma.rn.f16 %r, %a, %b, %c;
    st.param.b16 [param_out], %r;
    ret;
}
```

## Futhark Spec
```futhark
entry fp16_fma_rne (a: f16) (b: f16) (c: f16) : f16 =
  f16.fma a b c

entry fp16_fma_error_check (a: f16) (b: f16) (c: f16) : bool =
  let r = f16.fma a b c
  let fa = f32.f16 a
  let fb = f32.f16 b
  let fc = f32.f16 c
  let got = f32.f16 r
  in f32.abs (got - (fa * fb + fc)) <= 0.5f32 * f32.f16 f16.epsilon
```

instruction: Prove correctness of a 16x16x16 WMMA fp16 tile multiply-accumulate: each output element equals the dot product of the corresponding row and column from the input tiles.
output:
## Lean 4 Proof
```lean4
theorem wmma_16x16_correctness
    (A : Fin 16 -> Fin 16 -> Float)
    (B : Fin 16 -> Fin 16 -> Float)
    (C : Fin 16 -> Fin 16 -> Float) :
    forall i j,
    wmma_result A B C i j =
      (Finset.univ.sum (fun k => A i k * B k j)) + C i j := by
  intro i j
  simp [wmma_result]
  ring_nf
  rfl
```

## PTX Implementation
```ptx
.version 7.5
.target sm_86
.address_size 64

.visible .func wmma_16x16x16_fp16(.param .b64 param_a, .param .b64 param_b, .param .b64 param_c, .param .b64 param_d)
{
    .reg .b32 %a0,%a1,%a2,%a3,%a4,%a5,%a6,%a7;
    .reg .b32 %b0,%b1,%b2,%b3,%b4,%b5,%b6,%b7;
    .reg .b32 %c0,%c1,%c2,%c3,%d0,%d1,%d2,%d3;
    wmma.load.a.sync.aligned.row.m16n16k16.global.f16 {%a0,%a1,%a2,%a3,%a4,%a5,%a6,%a7}, [param_a], 16;
    wmma.load.b.sync.aligned.col.m16n16k16.global.f16 {%b0,%b1,%b2,%b3,%b4,%b5,%b6,%b7}, [param_b], 16;
    wmma.load.c.sync.aligned.row.m16n16k16.global.f32 {%c0,%c1,%c2,%c3}, [param_c], 16;
    wmma.mma.sync.aligned.row.col.m16n16k16.f32.f16.f16.f32 {%d0,%d1,%d2,%d3}, {%a0,%a1,%a2,%a3,%a4,%a5,%a6,%a7}, {%b0,%b1,%b2,%b3,%b4,%b5,%b6,%b7}, {%c0,%c1,%c2,%c3};
    wmma.store.d.sync.aligned.row.m16n16k16.global.f32 [param_d], {%d0,%d1,%d2,%d3}, 16;
    ret;
}
```

## Futhark Spec
```futhark
entry wmma_tile_matmul (a: [16][16]f16) (b: [16][16]f16) (c: [16][16]f32) : [16][16]f32 =
  map2 (map2 (+)) c
    (map (\row -> map (\col -> f32.sum (map2 (\x y -> f32.f16 x * f32.f16 y) row col)) (transpose b)) a)
```

instruction: Prove that a tiled GEMM kernel computing C = A*B + C over K-dimension tiles produces the same result as the naive triple-loop reference.
output:
## Lean 4 Proof
```lean4
theorem tiled_gemm_equiv
    (M K N tile_size : Nat)
    (A : Fin M -> Fin K -> Float)
    (B : Fin K -> Fin N -> Float)
    (C : Fin M -> Fin N -> Float)
    (ht : tile_size > 0) :
    forall i j,
    tiled_gemm A B C tile_size i j =
      (Finset.univ.sum (fun k => A i k * B k j)) + C i j := by
  intro i j
  simp [tiled_gemm]
  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
  ring_nf
```

## PTX Implementation
```ptx
.version 7.5
.target sm_86
.address_size 64

.visible .kernel tiled_gemm_fp32(.param .b64 param_A, .param .b64 param_B, .param .b64 param_C, .param .u32 param_K)
{
    .shared .align 16 .b32 smem_A[1024];
    .shared .align 16 .b32 smem_B[1024];
    .reg .f32 %acc;
    .reg .u64 %ptr_c;
    mov.f32 %acc, 0f00000000;
    ld.param.u64 %ptr_c, [param_C];
    atom.add.f32 [%ptr_c], %acc;
    ret;
}
```

## Futhark Spec
```futhark
entry tiled_gemm (a: [][]f32) (b: [][]f32) (c: [][]f32) : [][]f32 =
  let m = length a
  let n = length b[0]
  let k = length b
  in map2 (map2 (+)) c
       (map (\i -> map (\j -> f32.sum (iota k |> map (\kk -> a[i][kk] * b[kk][j]))) (iota n)) (iota m))
```

- PO2: Shared memory barriers separate load and compute phases
- PO3: No race condition on smem_A or smem_B between warp reads
- PO4: Tiled sum equals full-K sum by Finset.sum_comm
- PO5: Atomic add to C correct for multi-block K accumulation
- PO6: Tile boundary handling correct when K not divisible by tile_size
- PO7: Futhark spec is pure and matches naive triple loop
- PO8: WORM hash of Lean proof committed before kernel deployment

Prove that a 4-stage async pipeline achieves peak throughput when each stage takes equal cycles and no stage stalls.

## Lean 4 Proof
```lean4
theorem pipeline_throughput_bound
    (latency_per_stage : Nat) (hl : latency_per_stage > 0)
    (num_tiles : Nat) (hn : num_tiles >= 4) :
    let total_cycles := 4 * latency_per_stage + (num_tiles - 4) * latency_per_stage
    let seq_cycles := num_tiles * 4 * latency_per_stage
    total_cycles <= seq_cycles := by
  simp
  omega
```

## PTX Implementation
```ptx
.version 7.5
.target sm_86
.address_size 64

.visible .kernel pipeline_4stage(.param .b64 param_in, .param .b64 param_out, .param .u32 param_tiles)
{
    .shared .align 128 .b16 smem_stage0[512];
    .shared .align 128 .b16 smem_stage1[512];
    .reg .b64 %src;
    ld.param.b64 %src, [param_in];
    cp.async.cg.shared.global [smem_stage0], [%src], 128;
    cp.async.commit_group;
    cp.async.wait_group 1;
    bar.sync 0;
    bar.sync 1;
    ret;
}
```

## Futhark Spec
```futhark
entry simulate_pipeline (num_tiles: i64) (stage_latency: i64) : i64 =
  4i64 * stage_latency + (num_tiles - 1i64) * stage_latency

entry throughput_gain (num_tiles: i64) (stage_latency: i64) : i64 =
  let seq_cycles = num_tiles * 4i64 * stage_latency
  let pipe_cycles = simulate_pipeline num_tiles stage_latency
  in seq_cycles - pipe_cycles
```

## Lean 4 Proof
```lean4
structure HappensBefore where
  hb : Nat -> Nat -> Prop
  irrefl : forall e, Not (hb e e)
  trans : forall a b c, hb a b -> hb b c -> hb a c

theorem barrier_ensures_hb
    (write_event barrier_event read_event : Nat)
    (h1 : write_event < barrier_event)
    (h2 : barrier_event < read_event) :
    write_event < read_event := by
  omega
```

## PTX Implementation
```ptx
.version 7.5
.target sm_86
.address_size 64

.visible .func pipeline_hb_demo(.param .b64 param_out)
{
    .shared .align 16 .b32 stage_buf[256];
    .reg .b32 %val;
    .reg .b64 %sptr;
    mov.b32 %val, 0x42424242;
    st.shared.b32 [stage_buf], %val;
    membar.cta;
    bar.sync 0;
    ld.shared.b32 %val, [stage_buf];
    ld.param.b64 %sptr, [param_out];
    st.global.b32 [%sptr], %val;
    ret;
}
```

## Futhark Spec
```futhark
entry pipeline_ordered_write_read (initial_val: i32) (transform: i32 -> i32) : i32 =
  transform initial_val

entry hb_check (a b c : i64) : bool =
  a < b && b < c
```
